qualifiers.condition: Raising the timeout might require a reduction in the Region-level throttle quota; edge-optimized APIs are unchanged.

evidence.quote: Amazon API Gateway increased integration timeout limit — If you’re using Regional REST APIs and private REST APIs in Amazon API Gateway, now you can increase the integration timeout limit greater than 29 seconds.
| Integration timeout for edge-optimized APIs | 50 milliseconds - 29 seconds for all integration types, including Lambda, Lambda proxy, HTTP, HTTP proxy, and AWS integrations. | No |
evidence.table_header: | Resource or operation | Default quota | Can be increased |

note: Current truth: api-gateway-rest-timeout-regional, -private and -edge. Older exam questions assume a hard 29-second limit. The What's New page is blocked by robots.txt; the date comes from the change feed.

claim: On November 21, 2025 API Gateway began to support private integrations with Application Load Balancers for REST APIs. This removes the additional network hop that was previously required through a Network Load Balancer.
question: When could REST APIs first integrate privately with an Application Load Balancer, and what was required before?

evidence.quote: | [Private integration with Application Load Balancer](#history) | API Gateway now supports private integrations with Application Load Balancers for REST APIs. For more information, see [Private integrations for REST APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/private-integration.html). | November 21, 2025 |

This direct ALB integration delivers multiple advantages: reduced latency by eliminating the additional network hop previously required through Network Load Balancer, lower infrastructure costs through simplified architecture, and enhanced Layer 7 capabilities including HTTP/HTTPS health checks, advanced request-based routing, and native container service integration.

note: Current truth: api-gateway-vpclink-v2-rest-alb and api-gateway-vpclink-v1-legacy. Older questions say a REST private integration needs a Network Load Balancer.

claim: On 2026-09-08 API Gateway REST APIs gained mutual TLS for backend integrations: API Gateway can present an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to the backend instead of only a self-signed certificate that it generated. This is not examinable yet.
question: What changed for REST API backend integrations on September 8, 2026?

values.display: a self-signed certificate that it generated

qualifiers.condition: Generally available after 2026-07-15, so labelled not examinable yet.

evidence.quote: You can now configure Amazon API Gateway REST APIs to present an AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) certificate to your backend during the TLS handshake, enabling mutual TLS (mTLS). Previously, API Gateway could present only a self-signed certificate that it generated; now you can use a certificate signed by a certificate authority you trust.

evidence.heading: Amazon API Gateway now supports mutual TLS for backend integrations

changed.was: a self-signed certificate that it generated

note: not examinable yet (GA after 2026-07-15). Not in the guide pages or the history table saved in the corpus; evidence is the What's New post. Inbound mutual TLS for clients has existed since 2020-09-17.
